previous_disclosures.summary: Developing next-generation semiconductor products and manufacturing technologies involves risks such as challenging forecasts, unexpected delays from process complexity or material/equipment issues, and long diagnosis times for manufacturing defects, which can be serious and difficult to resolve.

Past delays in 10nm and 7nm technologies, as well as the 4th Gen Xeon delay, allowed competitors like TSMC to benefit from earlier process advancements, potentially causing greater adverse competitive impacts if future delays occur.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks in New Product Development and AI Execution
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD faces intense competition and rapid technological change in the AI market, with significant risks related to developing, qualifying, and shipping new products on time. Delays can cause missed customer design windows, while uncertainty in long-term AI adoption and potential failure to achieve return on investment pose material risks. The company cannot guarantee success against competitors like Nvidia or customers developing internal solutions, and product complexity necessitates successful high-value launches to maintain average selling prices and competitive positioning.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose risks related to the challenges of developing and qualifying new semiconductor products and technologies on time, and the competitive consequences of delays. Intel explicitly cites past delays in 10nm and 7nm processes that allowed competitors like TSMC to gain advantages, and notes limited market success with accelerator offerings. Similarly, AMD warns that failure to timely develop, qualify, or ship new products (including AI accelerators) could cause loss of competitive positioning and market share, and notes that substantial R&D investments do not guarantee timely implementation or customer acceptance.

sentences.text: These delays have allowed competitors using third-party foundries, such as TSMC, to benefit from advancements in manufacturing processes introduced ahead of us, including improvements in performance, energy efficiency, and other features, which have helped increase the competitiveness of their products.
On the product side, we have had limited market success with our accelerator offerings, and in 2024 we recognized $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.

If we fail to or are delayed in identifying, developing, qualifying or shipping new products or technologies that provide value to our customers and address these new trends, or if we fail to predict which new form factors, product features preferences or requirements consumers will adopt and adapt our business accordingly, we may lose competitive positioning, which could cause us to lose market share and require us to discount the selling prices of our products.

Although we make substantial investments in research and development, we cannot be certain that we will be able to develop, obtain or successfully implement new products and technologies on a timely basis or that they will be well-received by our customers.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Investment Risks and AI Technology Development
comparisons.peer_summary: Significant investments in research and development carry the risk of slow or unsuccessful returns, particularly in developing advanced technologies like custom AI accelerators and XPUs; failure to timely develop these or focus on non-adopted technologies could impair competitive position and negatively impact financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Avago highlight the risks associated with developing advanced technologies, specifically mentioning custom AI accelerators and the financial impact of unsuccessful R&D. Intel describes risks in forecasting and executing new manufacturing technologies and product delays, noting significant inventory charges for its Gaudi AI accelerators. Avago warns that failure to successfully develop advanced technologies, including ASICs like custom AI accelerators, could impair competitive position, and that slow or unsuccessful R&D efforts negatively impact financial results.

sentences.text: The development and implementation of new semiconductor products and manufacturing technologies are subject to many risks and uncertainties.
On the product side, we have had limited market success with our accelerator offerings, and in 2024 we recognized $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.
Failure to successfully develop increasingly advanced technologies, including ASICs such as custom AI accelerators or XPUs and other AI-related products, could impair our competitive position.
Increased investments in research and development, or slow or unsuccessful research and development efforts, would have a negative impact on our financial results.

comparisons.peer_topic: Technology advancement and cost reduction risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Rapid technological change and barriers to achieving acceptable yields for HBM and 3D memory, along with shrinking die sizes, create risks of shortened product life cycles, declining prices, and inability to recover R&D investments if competitors develop superior technologies.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron address the risks and uncertainties inherent in developing and implementing new semiconductor process technologies. Intel details challenges in using new materials/equipment and defects in advanced nodes (10nm, 7nm) that cause delays. Micron similarly notes that investing in new technologies like EUV lithography adds complexity and risk to schedules and costs, and that competitors developing superior technologies could render existing ones obsolete.

sentences.text: Forecasting our progress and schedule for developing advanced nodes and other technologies is challenging, and at times we encounter unexpected delays due to the complexity of interactions among steps in the manufacturing process, challenges in using new materials or new production equipment, and other issues.

We experienced significant delays in implementing our 10nm process technology, and in 2020, we encountered a defect mode in the development of our 7nm process technology that resulted in delays relative to our prior expectations.
We have invested and expect to continue to invest in R&D for new and existing products and process technologies, such as EUV lithography, to continue to deliver advanced product requirements.
Such new technologies can add complexity and risk to our schedule and may affect our costs and production output.

comparisons.peer_topic: Third-party supply chain dependencies and risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Nvidia depends on third-party suppliers, foundries, and subcontractors for manufacturing, assembly, testing, and procurement, lacking its own capabilities in these areas. This dependency reduces control over quantity, quality, yields, and delivery schedules. Risks include lack of guaranteed supply, foundry capacity failures, geographic concentration, supplier loss, quality failures, shipment delays, and natural disaster disruptions, which could adversely affect business operations, gross margin, and financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss risks related to third-party manufacturing and process technology implementation, though with different operational models. Intel, as an IDM, cites risks in its own manufacturing process (10nm, 7nm delays) and contrasts with competitors using third-party foundries. Nvidia, as a fabless company, explicitly discloses risks arising from its dependency on third-party foundries to develop and implement high-quality process technologies (e.g., advanced node transitions), noting that such failures could harm its business. Both identify the execution of advanced process nodes as a critical risk factor for competitive success.
